plan.title: Hallmark pathway activity scores: UC treated vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The question asks for a per-sample pathway activity score and a hallmark heatmap that shows which pathways separate the 6 UC-treated from the 6 control colon samples. The inputs are raw Salmon-derived gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples, symbol-keyed; counts.csv carries 13 columns = 1 gene-symbol column + 12 sample columns) plus a 12-row metadata table. Because many gene sets (the 50 MSigDB Hallmark sets) are scored across a fixed sample set and the group difference is tested on the score matrix, the knowledge procedure's alternative M-0034 (GSVA per-sample pathway scores with limma on the scores) is the right estimator; UCell (M-0045) is the per-signature default but is built for small signature lists, not a 50-set matrix test. GSVA scores are rank-based within a sample, so the ~4x-low-depth sample_01 is not depth-biased, but it is still kept, inspected on PCA/sample distances, and reported per rule R-0008. Flow: sample-structure QC -> minimal low-count filter and DESeq2 median-of-ratios normalization with a VST log-scale matrix -> GSVA on the VST matrix against the MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1 symbols GMT (sets intersected with the tested genes, 15-500 member window) -> limma on the 12 x 50 score matrix under ~condition with BH across the 50 sets, plus the annotated hallmark heatmap and per-pathway boxplots -> report with reproducibility record.
